programme.title: Journey Home
programme.desc:
Deacon Stephen Nash was baptized Catholic, but several of the family members who had been anchors of faith in his life passed away when he was young.
There were sparks of faith along the way that caused him to pop in and out of Church occasionally, especially in college, when he became friends with a classmate at Princeton who was discerning the priesthood.
When he married his wife, he started going to church regularly with her, but when their second child became ill, he really began to get serious about faith. That experience, combined with the persistent prayers of his Catholic family, were pivotal in him finally coming back fully to the sacraments, and eventually discerning a vocation to the diaconate.

programme.title: Journey Home
programme.desc:
Deacon Stephen Nash was baptized Catholic, but several of the family members who had been anchors of faith in his life passed away when he was young.
There were sparks of faith along the way that caused him to pop in and out of Church occasionally, especially in college, when he became friends with a classmate at Princeton who was discerning the priesthood.
When he married his wife, he started going to church regularly with her, but when their second child became ill, he really began to get serious about faith. That experience, combined with the persistent prayers of his Catholic family, were pivotal in him finally coming back fully to the sacraments, and eventually discerning a vocation to the diaconate.

programme.title: Journey Home
programme.desc:
Deacon Stephen Nash was baptized Catholic, but several of the family members who had been anchors of faith in his life passed away when he was young.
There were sparks of faith along the way that caused him to pop in and out of Church occasionally, especially in college, when he became friends with a classmate at Princeton who was discerning the priesthood.
When he married his wife, he started going to church regularly with her, but when their second child became ill, he really began to get serious about faith. That experience, combined with the persistent prayers of his Catholic family, were pivotal in him finally coming back fully to the sacraments, and eventually discerning a vocation to the diaconate.

programme.title: Journey Home
programme.desc:
Deacon Stephen Nash was baptized Catholic, but several of the family members who had been anchors of faith in his life passed away when he was young.
There were sparks of faith along the way that caused him to pop in and out of Church occasionally, especially in college, when he became friends with a classmate at Princeton who was discerning the priesthood.
When he married his wife, he started going to church regularly with her, but when their second child became ill, he really began to get serious about faith. That experience, combined with the persistent prayers of his Catholic family, were pivotal in him finally coming back fully to the sacraments, and eventually discerning a vocation to the diaconate.

When he married his wife, he started going to church regularly with her, but when their second child became ill, he really began to get serious about faith. That experience, combined with the persistent prayers of his Catholic family, were pivotal in him finally coming back fully to the sacraments, and eventually discerning a vocation to the diaconate.

programme.title: Journey Home
programme.desc:
Deacon Stephen Nash was baptized Catholic, but several of the family members who had been anchors of faith in his life passed away when he was young.
There were sparks of faith along the way that caused him to pop in and out of Church occasionally, especially in college, when he became friends with a classmate at Princeton who was discerning the priesthood.
When he married his wife, he started going to church regularly with her, but when their second child became ill, he really began to get serious about faith. That experience, combined with the persistent prayers of his Catholic family, were pivotal in him finally coming back fully to the sacraments, and eventually discerning a vocation to the diaconate.

programme.desc:
Deacon Stephen Nash was baptized Catholic, but several of the family members who had been anchors of faith in his life passed away when he was young.
There were sparks of faith along the way that caused him to pop in and out of Church occasionally, especially in college, when he became friends with a classmate at Princeton who was discerning the priesthood.
When he married his wife, he started going to church regularly with her, but when their second child became ill, he really began to get serious about faith. That experience, combined with the persistent prayers of his Catholic family, were pivotal in him finally coming back fully to the sacraments, and eventually discerning a vocation to the diaconate.

programme.title: Journey Home
programme.desc:
Deacon Stephen Nash was baptized Catholic, but several of the family members who had been anchors of faith in his life passed away when he was young.
There were sparks of faith along the way that caused him to pop in and out of Church occasionally, especially in college, when he became friends with a classmate at Princeton who was discerning the priesthood.
When he married his wife, he started going to church regularly with her, but when their second child became ill, he really began to get serious about faith. That experience, combined with the persistent prayers of his Catholic family, were pivotal in him finally coming back fully to the sacraments, and eventually discerning a vocation to the diaconate.

programme.title: Tertulias de fe
programme.desc: Criado en Bogotá, Colombia, Jerónimo creció en un hogar donde Jesús siempre fue el centro. El primer encuentro con Dios para Jerónimo fue un proceso gradual, marcado por la oración y el ejemplo de personas cercanas. Hoy, como sacerdote, Jerónimo encuentra su identidad y misión en el acompañamiento de los jóvenes. Inspirado por San José, busca sanar corazones y guiar a quienes están en búsqueda de sentido.

programme.title: Mientras el mundo gira
programme.desc: Pídele a Dios todos los días que no te suelte de su mano, que te ayude con su gracia a no pecar, a cambiar, que te lleve por el camino de la santidad. El Padre Willie nos pide que tratemos de definirnos sin Dios. ¿Quién nos da el oxígeno? Simplemente sin Él, no existiríamos. Demos gracias a Dios por ser y por estar, no dejemos de reconocer lo mucho que Él por amor nos da.

programme.title: Conozca primero su fe católica
programme.desc: Uno de los grandes amigos de Jesús se llamaba Lázaro, él era de Betania y tenía dos hermanas, María y Marta. Pero Lázaro se enferma. Sin embargo, Jesús se demora cuatro días y cuando llega ya Lázaro había muerto. Sin embargo Jesús va a verlo y cuando está frente a la tumba le dice a los que estaban alrededor: “¡Quiten esa piedra!” Y le dice a Lázaro: “¡Lázaro, levántate y sal fuera!” Lázaro opta por salir y el Señor le da vida nueva. Eso es lo que quiere hacer Dios contigo el día de hoy también. El P. Núñez también responde a las preguntas llegadas al programa vía telefónica, el correo electrónico (padrepedro@ewtn.com) y Facebook (www.facebook.com/ppedronunez).

programme.title: La pasión, análisis médico
programme.desc: La Pasión de Jesús nos conmueve por el nivel de sufrimiento que experimenta el Señor, al tiempo que manifiesta su gran amor por cada uno de nosotros, haciendo del dolor un instrumento de Salvación. ¿Cómo fue el dolor físico que experimentó el Señor durante su Pasión? ¿Cómo fue el dolor en el Corazón que experimento Jesús durante su Pasión? También son cofundadores del ministerio Renovación Familiar (Family Renewal Minstries, Inc.), un ministerio dedicado a servir a matrimonios y familias en los Estados Unidos y Latinoamérica. Ricardo y Lucia han trabajado extensamente como directores en varias arquidiócesis de Estados Unidos en las áreas de laicado, matrimonio, vida familiar, pastoral hispana y vida parroquial. Ellos han producido y presentado cientos de retiros, talleres, conferencias, congresos, programas y cursos en español. También son escritores para varias publicadoras católicas. Además anfitriones en EWTN Radio Católica Mundial y por EWTN Español.

programme.desc: Criado en Bogotá, Colombia, Jerónimo creció en un hogar donde Jesús siempre fue el centro. El primer encuentro con Dios para Jerónimo fue un proceso gradual, marcado por la oración y el ejemplo de personas cercanas. Hoy, como sacerdote, Jerónimo encuentra su identidad y misión en el acompañamiento de los jóvenes. Inspirado por San José, busca sanar corazones y guiar a quienes están en búsqueda de sentido.

programme.title: Mientras el mundo gira
programme.desc: Pídele a Dios todos los días que no te suelte de su mano, que te ayude con su gracia a no pecar, a cambiar, que te lleve por el camino de la santidad. El Padre Willie nos pide que tratemos de definirnos sin Dios. ¿Quién nos da el oxígeno? Simplemente sin Él, no existiríamos. Demos gracias a Dios por ser y por estar, no dejemos de reconocer lo mucho que Él por amor nos da.

programme.title: Conozca primero su fe católica
programme.desc: Uno de los grandes amigos de Jesús se llamaba Lázaro, él era de Betania y tenía dos hermanas, María y Marta. Pero Lázaro se enferma. Sin embargo, Jesús se demora cuatro días y cuando llega ya Lázaro había muerto. Sin embargo Jesús va a verlo y cuando está frente a la tumba le dice a los que estaban alrededor: “¡Quiten esa piedra!” Y le dice a Lázaro: “¡Lázaro, levántate y sal fuera!” Lázaro opta por salir y el Señor le da vida nueva. Eso es lo que quiere hacer Dios contigo el día de hoy también. El P. Núñez también responde a las preguntas llegadas al programa vía telefónica, el correo electrónico (padrepedro@ewtn.com) y Facebook (www.facebook.com/ppedronunez).

Hoy, como sacerdote, Jerónimo encuentra su identidad y misión en el acompañamiento de los jóvenes. Inspirado por San José, busca sanar corazones y guiar a quienes están en búsqueda de sentido.

programme.title: Mientras el mundo gira
programme.desc: Pídele a Dios todos los días que no te suelte de su mano, que te ayude con su gracia a no pecar, a cambiar, que te lleve por el camino de la santidad. El Padre Willie nos pide que tratemos de definirnos sin Dios. ¿Quién nos da el oxígeno? Simplemente sin Él, no existiríamos. Demos gracias a Dios por ser y por estar, no dejemos de reconocer lo mucho que Él por amor nos da.

programme.title: Tertulias de fe
programme.desc: Dr. Ricardo Luzondo y Lucía Báez Luzondo, JD. MAPT son cofundadores y directores de pastoral Hispania para Marriage Building USA / Construyendo Matrimonios USA, Inc. También son cofundadores del ministerio Renovación Familiar (Family Renewal Minstries, Inc.), un ministerio dedicado a servir a matrimonios y familias en los Estados Unidos y Latinoamérica. Ricardo y Lucia han trabajado extensamente como directores en varias arquidiócesis de Estados Unidos en las áreas de laicado, matrimonio, vida familiar, pastoral hispana y vida parroquial. Ellos han producido y presentado cientos de retiros, talleres, conferencias, congresos, programas y cursos en español. También son escritores para varias publicadoras católicas. Además anfitriones en EWTN Radio Católica Mundial y por EWTN Español.
